text:
Tori: quick follow-up from the quant-profiles RFC: we saw a mismatch where the loader applied tokenwise 4-bit packing after runtime had chosen attention kernels -> runtime crashed. Need a micro-protocol to avoid this.
Dev: ouch. sounds like we need a pre-bind "profile assertion" step so loader can say: "I may rewrite kv-encoding and bitwidths".
Nikhil: propose tiny flow: loader calls runtime.assert_quant_surface(manifest_header) -> runtime returns OK/REJECT + reason. If OK, runtime reserves kernels for declared bitwidths.
Tori: love it. keep it cheap (no allocation) for CI/preflight; optionally runtime.reserve_kernels() if loader asks.
Dev: what about safety? if loader later mutates more than declared, runtime should either refuse live mutation or require explicit rebind.
Nikhil: yes: two actions: ASSERT (cheap check), RESERVE (allocate kernels), REBIND (full reselection). Manifest fields: assert_only bool, allowed_bitwidths, max_rebind_ms, hysteresis_ms.
Tori: telemetry: assert_latency_ms, reserve_success, rebind_count, assert_failures. Ops alert if assert_fail_rate > 1% in 5m.
RuntimeBot: canary: "handshake assert flow v1 deployed to canary" :rocket:
Dev: I'll put a small appendix in the RFC and open a PR for the handshake proto today. Tori/Nikhil can we aim for canary Mon?
Tori: yes will add SRE alerts. Nikhil: i'll write unit tests for assert vs reserve vs rebind. Closing thread.
